text.p: Victorian betting agency and gaming firm Tabcorp Holdings Ltd said growth in its leisure and entertainment markets would continue to outpace the economy.
The company, which was sold by the state government of Victoria in 1994, said it would meet this growth in demand through the expansion and enhancement of its products and distribution network.

"At the same time, the company continues to generate strong cash flows which will allow for investments to be made should suitable opportunities arise," managing director Ross Wilson said in a statement accompanying the 1996/97 first half result.
The company reported a 17.5 percent rise in net profit to A$51.21 million and a 16.4 percent rise in pre-tax operating profit to A$79.80 million.
Tabcorp said the profit rise was driven by its gaming division, which also achieved higher sales. The wagering division had lower earnings and sales.
Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) in the gaming division rose 27.6 percent to A$58.2 million and sales rose by 21.1 percent to A$250.5 million.
In the wagering division, EBIT fell by 9.8 percent to A$17.9 million and sales fell by 1.9 percent to A$159.1 million.
